correspondence.finding: The starting vertex lies in the small feeder setting immediately west of Puentecita. The original sheet shows the short connecting stream network and its southward continuation into the corridor labeled Quebrada Jalegua. The initial tiny feeder has no separately established name; the modeled vertex is not asserted to be the official source of Jalegua or Aguán.

The route continues south through Quebrada Jalegua, then bends southwest and west along Río Jalegua through the Chalmeca and northern Yoro setting. The map separately shows Quebrada Jalegüita, Quebrada Honda and Río Machigua as joining waterways; their names are not transferred to the selected Jalegua route.

West of Yoro, Río Jalegua joins the named Aguán arriving from the south. The selected route turns north along Aguán past the Molunga, La Laguna Mansa, Río Abajo, San Isidro and San José setting. It does not continue upstream along the separate southern Aguán branch.

Aguán continues through the southern Jimiá sheet, turns northeast and east, and emerges into the broad valley on the Arenal sheet. The selected eastward corridor follows repeated Aguán labels past Arenal and Santa Cruz toward Olanchito. The modeled bends simplify the mapped confined valley and floodplain channel without selecting a different named branch.

The route follows Aguán past El Cayo and south of Olanchito, distinct from the Yaguala and Agalteca approaches. On the San Francisco sheet both selected fragments occupy the same Aguán corridor across their split; the route passes the Río Mame junction and continues past Campo Nuevo. The model split is not a natural name boundary.

Below Campo Nuevo the selection follows Aguán along the southern Sonaguera sheet toward Sabá, then northeast through the Prieta, Masicales and Guapinol setting. The Ilanga sheet resolves the short intervening Aguán Paso Tocoa and La Lima reach before the Corocito sheet. Tributaries and floodplain canals are visibly separate.

The lower selection follows the Aguán floodplain through Quebrada de Arena and west of Corocito, then east across the northern Bonito Oriental sheet into the Santa Rosa de Aguán sheet. The sources show the continuous named river and its large meanders. Nearby lagoons and the Río Bonito tributary remain separate features; the simplified line is not used to assign their names to the river.

On the coastal plain the Aguán corridor turns north, then northwest toward Santa Rosa de Aguán. The selected tip lies on the lower river immediately inland of its mapped mouth between Barra de Aguán and Santa Rosa de Aguán. It is not the separate Río Chapagua outlet farther west, the Laguna El Lirio/Crique El Lirio network, or offshore Caribbean water. No exact contemporary shoreline endpoint is asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwestern approach and local Arroyo el Hormiguero
correspondence.finding: The starting selection lies in mapped terrain subject to inundation southwest of La Huasteca. Part of its northeastern approach shares the intermittent-channel setting labeled A. el Hormiguero. The modeled route subsequently continues through the Tepeyac–Bel-Há and X-Panzil surroundings, beyond the scope established by that local hydronym. The original distinguishes nearby independent short arroyos; their names are not assigned to the selected connector.

Across the Chetumal/Felipe Carrillo Puerto sheet boundary the actual selection passes the Río Verde settlement setting and extensive inundation-prone terrain. Readable original mapping does not show a single continuous channel tracking the entire modeled interval. Río Verde is a locality label here and cannot supply a river name merely because the selection passes it.

The central selection crosses the Monte Olivo–Valle Hermoso surroundings, then runs toward the Lago Sac-Ayin and Timul setting. The original maps show broad flood-prone areas and separate lakes, minor channels and dry intervening terrain. Local lake names are geographic anchors; a continuous named river linking all these features is not established.

The selected northern loop bends across the Chancah Derrepente–San Andrés surroundings and then south through the Lago Kaam–Lago X-Hazil area. These intervals are readable on the original sheet but are not represented as one continuous river corresponding to the modeled loop. No lake name is extended over the intervening land or treated as a whole-system alias.

The eastern selection bends northeast and east across extensive terrain marked as swamp and land subject to inundation, then turns southeast to a terminal point within marsh west of Bahía del Espíritu Santo. Original bay-context pixels distinguish Boca de Xoquene and Los Tres Reyes along the bay side. They do not name one watercourse matching the entire selected marsh crossing or establish the terminal vertex as a surveyed river mouth.

The INEGI compendium distinguishes an inland Cuencas Cerradas basin from the coastal Bahías La Ascensión y Espíritu Santo subbasin. Its regional map and tables reinforce that inland flood-prone and coastal settings must not automatically be merged into a single named surface river. They do not establish the precise position of a basin boundary along this selection.

correspondence.component_scope: Northwestern descent and stepped eastward upper-middle course
correspondence.finding: The route first descends nearly south, turns southeast, and then follows a stepped eastward course with short level intervals. Comparison with the original graticule places this opening and upper-middle course on the eastern continental Inland Ice, inland of the mountain margin. No corresponding named natural river is established.

correspondence.component_scope: Long south-southeastward middle limb and lower turn east
correspondence.finding: A marked south-southeastward descent, with a long straight diagonal and a short nearly north-south interval, carries the selection toward the glaciated margin before the line turns east again. Its straight and stair-stepped intervals belong to the modeled inventory geometry. The original map distinguishes the ice-interior contours from the irregular marginal glacier and exposed-rock pattern; those contours do not independently map a river along the selection.

correspondence.component_scope: Long eastward terminal limb and actual southeastern ending
correspondence.finding: The final limb continues predominantly eastward with successive small southward steps, long nearly level intervals and a short final southward tip. The regional and terminal crops place this part in the glaciated mountain-margin setting south-southwest of Kap Edvard Holm, rather than at Kangerdlugssuaq fjord. The sheet shows glacier corridors interspersed with exposed geological units toward the coast. It supplies no named natural-river correspondence for this limb and does not warrant assigning an exact named terminal feature or present-day river mouth.

correspondence.component_scope: Whole selected mainstem and cartographic feature class
correspondence.finding: One mainstem and no tributary geometry are selected; internal MultiLineString parts were considered together. Neither original establishes one continuously named natural river across the complete ice-interior-to-margin selection. The legend identifies blue surface contours, dashed ice-thickness isopachs, sub-ice bedrock contours and aeromagnetic lineaments. These are not river traces. The lineament convention applies only south of 68°N and is relevant to interpreting symbols in the southern part, not to proving a river.

The southern end lies in the São Brás de Cima–Tenente Ananias drainage. The detailed municipal map shows the northwest-running waterway past Tenente Ananias labeled Rio São Brás. Its subsequent northward connection is visible; the modeled endpoint is not identified as the official source of São Brás or Apodi.

After the northwestern bend, the selected route runs north and northeast through the Marcelino Vieira setting, bends northwest toward Pau dos Ferros and continues north. The regional sheet places Rio Apodi labels on this receiving corridor. It separately depicts the western Encanto approach and eastern Rio Pilões drainage.

The route turns northeast past São Francisco do Oeste and Taboleiro Grande, follows the Rio Apodi corridor south of Itaú, and enters the large impounded southwestern arm. The municipal map shows the actual river-to-reservoir connection; the SGB sheet distinguishes this from the southern Riacho das Marrecas approach.

The selection crosses the main impoundment northeastward and northward to its eastern outlet setting. Readable SGB pixels label the water body Barragem Santa Cruz do Apodi. The western Riacho Mansidão arm and other side arms are not separate selected branches, and the reservoir name is not a river alias.

Below the impoundment, the line continues north past Santa Rosa and bends northwest toward the eastern side of Apodi before turning northeast. Both detailed maps distinguish Lagoa do Apodi extending west from the town from the selected river corridor to the east and southeast. The selection does not traverse the lagoon's long western body.

The middle and lower selection follows the repeatedly labeled Rio Apodi northeast past Felipe Guerra and Governador Dix-Sept Rosado, then through Mossoró. The regional map distinguishes the approaching Umari, Carmo and other side drainages from that continuous selected corridor.

Downstream of Mossoró, the selected northeastern line enters the mapped estuary, bends through the Grossos setting and runs north beside Areia Branca to the coastal outlet. The terminal setting is supported, while individual tidal-channel names and an exact modern shoreline intersection are not established.

scope_limit: MAIN_RIV groups and model mainstem roles do not establish a uniform name for every included reach, tributary or lake passage. Source observations support only the stated representative identity or hold.
publication_boundary: Own factual observations, attribution and official public URLs only; source originals, images, complete coordinates and private evidence remain omitted.
